intervals.label: 80-inch chamber initial run
intervals.locator: BNL 'Our History: Accelerators', 80-inch Bubble Chamber section
intervals.note: The CERN Courier says the omega-minus was sought "in the initial run of the 80 inch bubble chamber", so the experiment is taken to start with the chamber's first photograph. The end is the bound of the completed interval.
intervals.quote: When its first photograph of particle interactions was taken in June 1963, the 80-inch bubble chamber was the largest such detector in the world.

intervals.label: completed
intervals.note: A bound, not an end-of-run date: the discovery analysis was complete when the paper was submitted. The 80-inch chamber ran a much longer programme that is outside this record.
intervals.quote: 11 February A Brookhaven National Laboratory team submits “Observation of a hyperon with strangeness minus three” to Physical Review Letters

key_specs.label: Events reported in the discovery paper

quantity.quote: With 33 authors, it reported only one event.

name: AGS 80-inch bubble chamber omega-minus experiment
notes: No collaboration record: a 33-author Brookhaven team with Syracuse and Rochester members on the author list; the Atlas has no sourced collaboration name. No detector record for the 80-inch chamber (not assigned to this stream).
BNL's Omega group takes its name from this discovery (BNL Physics Division, Omega group page).
The beam used for the exposure was not stated in any source fetched, so no beam spec is recorded.

physics_goals.quote: Brookhaven experimenter Nick Samios was eagerly seeking evidence of this very strange particle in the initial run of the 80 inch bubble chamber that he and colleagues had spent years planning and building.
physics_goals.value: Find the strangeness -3 baryon predicted by Gell-Mann in a bubble-chamber exposure

summary.plain: A Brookhaven team led by Nicholas Samios searched the first run of the lab's new 80-inch bubble chamber for a particle predicted by Murray Gell-Mann. On 31 January 1964 they found one photograph that showed it, the omega-minus, and the pattern it completed held up.
summary.technical: Bubble-chamber exposure at the AGS in the initial run of the 80-inch chamber; a single event, found on 31 January 1964 and submitted to PRL on 11 February 1964, established the strangeness -3 hyperon predicted by SU(3) flavour symmetry.
